처음 뵙겠습니다.forms: formal set phrase · friendlier: 만나서 반가워요
처음 뵙겠습니다.m: how do you do?, nice to meet you (lit. I see you for the first time)
처음 뵙겠습니다.x: How do you do? I'm Kim Minsu.
처음 뵙겠습니다.e: Literally 'I will see you for the first time'; 뵙다 is the humble form of 보다 (to see).
처음 뵙겠습니다.t: Very polite, for formal first meetings. Usually followed by your name and 잘 부탁드립니다.

여보세요.t: Only for phone calls. 여보 on its own means 'honey/dear' between spouses!

언제.e: Add 나 and get 언제나 'always'; 언제든지 = 'anytime'.

마리.forms: native number + 마리: 고양이 두 마리
마리.ex: 우리 집에는 강아지가 한 마리 있어요.
마리.x: We have one puppy at our house.
마리.e: For animals and fish: 고양이 두 마리 = two cats. Chicken places sell chicken by the 마리 (whole bird).

허리.x: My lower back hurts because I sat for a long time.
허리.t: 허리 covers both the waist and the lower back: 허리가 아파요 usually means 'My back hurts.'

현금.x: At the market it's better to pay in cash.

한글.e: 글 = writing; 한 probably 'great' or 'Korean'. Created by King Sejong in 1443; name coined about 1912.
한글.t: 한글 is the writing system, not the language — the language is 한국어.

신다.m: to wear, to put on (shoes, socks)
신다.x: I put on sneakers and went out.
신다.e: Related to 신 (shoes), as in 신발. Used for shoes and socks.
신다.t: Pronounced [신따]: the ending tenses after ㄴ in verb stems.

아마.forms: 아마 + -(으)ㄹ 거예요: 아마 비가 올 거예요
아마.e: 아마 비가 올 거예요 (It'll probably rain).
아마.t: Usually paired with a guess ending like -(으)ㄹ 거예요.

또는.forms: between nouns: A 또는 B · in speech often 아니면 or -(이)나
또는.x: Shall I get you coffee or tea?
또는.e: 또 (also) + 는. In casual speech 아니면 often replaces it.
또는.t: Somewhat formal; in conversation 커피나 차 is more common.

치과.ex: 이가 아파서 내일 치과에 가야 해요.
치과.x: My tooth hurts, so I have to go to the dentist tomorrow.
치과.e: Literally 'tooth department'; -과 = medical department: 치과, 안과, 내과.

기대하다.m: to look forward to, to expect
기대하다.x: I'm really looking forward to the weekend trip.
기대하다.t: 기대돼요! 'I can't wait!' is the most natural way to show excitement about plans.

기말고사.x: Vacation starts right after finals are over.

어머.x: Oh my, is it already this late?
어머.e: Stretched to 어머나 for extra surprise.
어머.t: 어머 tends to sound feminine; men more often say 어, 와 or 아이고.

사자.x: People call the lion the king of animals.

관계.x: I have good relationships with my coworkers.

잔치.ex: 할머니 생신에 온 가족이 모여서 잔치를 했어요.
잔치.x: The whole family got together and threw a party for Grandma's birthday.
잔치.e: A native word for a big celebration with food, as in 돌잔치 and 잔치국수 'banquet noodles'.
잔치.t: Noodles were served at weddings, so 국수 언제 먹여 줄 거예요? jokingly asks 'When are you getting married?'

실패.ex: 실패를 두려워하지 말고 다시 해 보세요.
실패.x: Don't be afraid of failure; try again.
실패.t: 실수 is a small slip; 실패 is failing at a goal.

환불하다.m: to refund, to give a refund
환불하다.ex: 영수증이 있으면 일주일 안에 환불해 드려요.
환불하다.x: If you have the receipt, we'll give you a refund within a week.
환불하다.t: As a customer, say 환불받고 싶어요 'I'd like a refund'; the store 환불해 드려요.

대표이사.x: The new CEO greeted the employees today.
대표이사.e: Literally 'representative director' — the officially registered head of a Korean company.
대표이사.t: Business cards often translate 대표이사 as CEO; in conversation people usually say 사장님 or 대표님.

가계.x: Rising prices have increased the burden on household finances.
가계.e: Literally 'house calculation' — a family's money matters.
가계.t: Often pronounced [가게], so it can sound just like 가게 (store) — context tells them apart.

부채.e: Literally 'carry a debt'. Homonym: native 부채 means a hand fan.
부채.t: In daily speech people say 빚; 부채 is the news and finance word.

파산.x: That company finally went bankrupt last year.
파산.t: 파산 신청 = filing for bankruptcy; it works for both people and companies.

불공평하다.ex: 나만 매일 청소를 하는 건 불공평해요.
불공평하다.x: It's unfair that I'm the only one who cleans every day.

전해지다.m: to be reported, to be conveyed; to be handed down
전해지다.ex: 그 배우가 다음 달에 결혼하는 것으로 전해졌습니다.
전해지다.x: The actor is reported to be getting married next month.
전해지다.e: 전하다 'to pass on' + -어지다 'become': to get passed on.
전해지다.t: News reports often end with ~것으로 전해졌습니다 'it is reported that…'.

문화유산.x: Hanok houses are a precious part of Korea's cultural heritage.

연체.ex: 카드 값을 연체하면 신용 점수가 떨어져요.
연체.x: If you're late on your card payments, your credit score drops.
연체.e: Literally 'delayed and stuck': a payment that hasn't moved on time.

언짢다.m: upset, displeased, in a bad mood
언짢다.ex: 아버지는 제 대답을 듣고 언짢은 표정을 지으셨어요.
언짢다.x: My father made a displeased face when he heard my answer.
언짢다.t: Pronounced [언짠타]; ㄶ before ㄷ makes an aspirated ㅌ.

무료하다.m: bored, idle, with nothing to do
무료하다.ex: 병원에 입원해 있는 동안 너무 무료했어요.
무료하다.x: While I was in the hospital, I was so bored.
무료하다.t: Homonym warning: 무료 입장 means 'free admission', not 'boring admission'.

뛰어들다.forms: 뛰어들어요 · 뛰어들었어요 · 뛰어들 거예요 · 뛰어드세요 (ㄹ drops)
뛰어들다.m: to jump into, to dive in; to plunge into (a field)
뛰어들다.x: He jumped into the river to save the child.

모호하다.x: The question is too vague to answer.

분주하다.x: Before the holidays, the market is bustling with people.

해시태그.ex: 사진을 올릴 때 해시태그를 꼭 달아요.
해시태그.x: I always add hashtags when I post photos.
해시태그.t: Add one is 해시태그를 달다/붙이다; Koreans read the # sign as 샵 ('sharp').

운세.x: Every morning I check my horoscope for the day on my phone.
운세.e: Literally 'luck trend': the way one's fortune is going.
운세.t: 신년 운세 'fortune for the new year' is popular in January; newspapers and apps often list daily fortunes by Chinese zodiac animal (띠).

국수를 먹다.forms: 언제 국수 먹여 줄 거예요? · 국수를 먹게 되다
국수를 먹다.m: to get married, to hold a wedding; to attend someone's wedding (lit. to eat noodles)
국수를 먹다.ex: 두 분 사귄 지 오래됐는데 언제 국수 먹여 줄 거예요?
국수를 먹다.x: You two have been dating for a long time. When are you getting married?
국수를 먹다.e: Noodle soup (잔치국수) was traditionally served to wedding guests, and long noodles stand for a long life together.
국수를 먹다.t: Mostly in the teasing question 언제 국수 먹여 줄 거예요? 'When are you treating us to noodles?', asked to someone single or in a long relationship.

혼술.ex: 퇴근하고 집에서 맥주 한 캔으로 혼술했어요.
혼술.x: After work I had a can of beer by myself at home.
혼술.t: Casual. Usually means a relaxed drink at home rather than heavy drinking.

밀도.ex: 서울은 인구 밀도가 매우 높은 도시예요.
밀도.x: Seoul is a city with a very high population density.

운문.x: Sijo is a representative form of Korean verse literature.
운문.t: 운문 vs 산문 (verse vs prose) is a classic pair on Korean literature exams.

노련하다.x: The player led the game with veteran skill.
노련하다.e: Literally 'old and tempered' — skill refined over many years.
노련하다.t: 노련미 means 'the skill of a veteran', often said of athletes and actors.

눈살을 찌푸리다.forms: 눈살을 찌푸려요 · 눈살을 찌푸렸어요 · 눈살을 찌푸리게 하다
눈살을 찌푸리다.m: to frown; to scowl in disapproval
눈살을 찌푸리다.ex: 지하철에서 큰 소리로 통화해서 사람들이 눈살을 찌푸렸어요.
눈살을 찌푸리다.x: He talked loudly on the phone on the subway, so people frowned.
눈살을 찌푸리다.e: 눈살 = the wrinkles between the eyebrows, from 눈 'eye.'

열을 올리다.forms: 열을 올려요 · 열을 올렸어요 · ~에 열을 올리다
열을 올리다.m: to go all out on; to get fired up about; to get heated
열을 올리다.ex: 요즘 회사들이 인공지능 개발에 열을 올리고 있습니다.
열을 올리다.x: These days, companies are going all out on AI development.
열을 올리다.e: Literally 'to raise the heat' — getting fired up.

지위.x: She rose to a high position at the company.
지위.e: Literally 'ground position' — the place you occupy.

세출.ex: 정부는 내년 세출 규모를 늘리기로 했습니다.
세출.x: The government decided to increase next year's spending.
세출.e: Literally 'what goes out during the year'.

온돌.ex: 겨울에는 따뜻한 온돌방에서 자는 게 최고예요.
온돌.x: In winter, sleeping in a warm ondol room is the best.
온돌.e: Literally 'warm' + 'flue': smoke from a fire flows through channels under stone floors.

교화.ex: 교도소의 목적은 처벌뿐 아니라 교화에도 있습니다.
교화.x: The purpose of prison lies not only in punishment but also in reform.

인륜.m: basic human morality, moral duties between people
인륜.ex: 부모를 버리는 것은 인륜에 어긋나는 일이에요.
인륜.x: Abandoning your parents goes against basic human morality.
인륜.e: Literally 'human order': the proper relations between people.
인륜.t: Pronounced [일륜]: ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

포교.ex: 그 스님은 해외 포교를 위해 미국으로 떠났어요.
포교.x: The monk left for America to spread Buddhism overseas.

구원.ex: 많은 사람들이 종교에서 영혼의 구원을 찾아요.
구원.x: Many people seek salvation for their souls in religion.
구원.t: A homonym 구원 means 'an old grudge', as in 구원을 풀다; context tells them apart.

내세.ex: 많은 종교가 내세에 대한 믿음을 가지고 있어요.
내세.x: Many religions hold a belief in the afterlife.

부정맥.ex: 건강검진 때 받은 심전도 검사에서 부정맥이 발견되었습니다.
부정맥.x: An arrhythmia was found on the ECG I had during my checkup.

점철되다.m: to be dotted with, to be marked by (a series of events)
점철되다.x: His life was marked by failure and frustration.
점철되다.e: Literally 'dotted and stitched together' — a life strung with events.
점철되다.t: Pattern: N(으)로 점철되다, usually with negative things like 실패, 갈등, 고난.

결부하다.m: to link, to connect, to tie (to)
결부하다.ex: 그 사건을 정치 문제와 결부해서 생각하면 안 돼요.
결부하다.x: You shouldn't link that incident to political issues.

심오하다.ex: 이 시에는 삶에 대한 심오한 의미가 담겨 있어요.
심오하다.x: This poem contains a profound meaning about life.

절묘하다.ex: 그 선수는 절묘한 타이밍에 골을 넣었어요.
절묘하다.x: That player scored a goal with perfect timing.
절묘하다.t: Great for timing and balance: 절묘한 타이밍, 절묘한 조화.

바야흐로.m: now (at last), just now, at this very moment
바야흐로.x: The age of artificial intelligence has now truly arrived.
바야흐로.e: A grand, literary 'now' used to announce a new era or season.
바야흐로.t: Typical frame: 바야흐로 ~의 계절이다/시대다 'it is now the season/age of ~'.

탄소배출.x: The government announced it would greatly cut carbon emissions by 2030.
탄소배출.t: Collocation: 탄소배출을 줄이다 or 감축하다 'to cut carbon emissions'.

보좌하다.x: He assisted the president closely for ten years.
보좌하다.t: Used only for helping someone higher up; 보좌관 is a lawmaker's aide.

열람하다.m: to read, to view, to look over (records)
열람하다.ex: 도서관에서는 옛날 신문을 무료로 열람할 수 있어요.
열람하다.x: You can view old newspapers for free at the library.

혼선.ex: 발표 내용이 자주 바뀌어서 현장에 혼선이 생겼습니다.
혼선.x: The announcement kept changing, which caused confusion on site.
혼선.e: Literally 'mixed lines', like crossed telephone wires; now any mix-up in communication.
혼선.t: Common collocations: 혼선을 빚다 and 혼선이 생기다 'cause/have a mix-up'.
